sources.title: USGS MSL Gale Merged DEM v3 · Parker & Calef, 2016
sources.note: Local grids are nearest-neighbour samples from the official 1 m-grid GeoTIFF. Source detail varies: HiRISE, CTX, HRSC, then MOLA. Source bounds verified from the GeoTIFF: 137.124166506–137.680559054° E, −5.098652339 to −4.129604796° N. Source NoData is −32767. The 12 × 9 km display grid has 196,608/196,608 valid sampled cells; the 40 × 30 km coverage view has 222,466/307,200 (72.42%). These counts describe sampled grid cells, not every source pixel or a full 20 km-radius circle. Credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech, USGS, University of Arizona; HRSC from ESA/DLR/FU Berlin.

sources.title: USGS Gale merged orthophoto v3 · Calef & Parker, 2016
sources.note: Bundled grayscale crop at 11.72 m display spacing, nearest-sampled from the official 25 cm-grid mosaic. Raster transform and bounds verified against the DEM coordinate frame. 775,123 of 786,432 sampled cells (98.56%) have imagery; transparent imagery gaps show DEM relief. The displayed green-brown tint is cartographic, not true colour. Coverage view uses DEM relief only. Original source detail and positional accuracy vary. Full processing metadata is in imagery-provenance.json.

sources.title: Curiosity landing reconstruction · NASA NTRS, 2013
sources.note: Display centre: 4.5895° S, 137.4417° E. The brief's 5.4° S, 137.8° E centre is outside the merged DEM. Habitat and crew route are fictional, not Curiosity's traverse.

sources.title: Mars surface radiation · Hassler et al., Science, 2014
sources.note: Table 1 reports a 2012–2013 GCR tissue-like E-detector absorbed dose rate of 0.21 ± 0.04 mGy/day. Marswalk uses 210 µGy/Earth day as a uniform illustrative reference, with no personal-dose, altitude, pressure, or shielding model. The observed historical reference is distinguished from its estimated map-wide application.

sources.title: Radiation measurements on Mars · NASA/JPL-Caltech/SwRI
sources.note: NASA's 2013 description gives about 210 micrograys per day for GCR absorbed dose. This is historical context, not today's radiation or a safety threshold.

sources.title: REMS archive · NASA PDS Atmospheres Node
sources.note: No REMS tables are included. Temperature and pressure are explicitly simulated formulas, spatially uniform. Thermal inertia, ground temperature, season dependence, and elevation correction are not modeled.

sources.title: Marswalk simulation fixtures
sources.note: Fictional 8.67 km loop, habitat, astronaut, and sol-004 clock. Traverse takes place from 08:00 to 12:00 simulated local time. The manual solar-event alert changes no physical reading. No sourced safety thresholds or route-hazard assessment are provided.

sources.title: NASA JPL Mars Trek — Viking regional context
sources.note: Bundled 16 tiles from Viking MDIM 2.1 colorized WMTS level 7, rows 66–69, columns 224–227. Bounds read from the published matrix origin and dimensions. NASA/JPL, USGS, NASA Ames, Viking Orbiter. Regional image sampling approximately 325 m; no elevation inferred.

sources.title: Curiosity’s Proposed Path up Mount Sharp
sources.note: Reference for map presentation. The displayed astronaut loop is a fictional training route, not this proposed Curiosity route.

sources.title: NASA Worldview
sources.note: Earth imagery viewer; used as an interaction reference only, not a Mars dataset.

sources.title: Perseverance science and imagery
sources.note: Perseverance explores Jezero Crater. Its raw photographs are not substituted for georeferenced Gale imagery.
